newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Exchange rate helps Czech March trade data - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Exchange rate helps Czech March trade data - analyst.

text.p: Czech March trade figures were positive, but do not indicate a turnaround in the trend of a widening gap between imports and exports, investment house Wood and Company said on Wednesday.

Speaking to Reuters at the FIBEX banking and finance fair in the Czech city of Brno, Jiri Krovak, head of Wood and Company's economic research department said a lot of the better-than-expected March data was due to exchange rate movements.
"The figures were positive, but I think a lot of it can be explained by the change in the exchange rate," he said.
"The average exchange rate in March compared to February was about 3.5 percent weaker. This explains about 75 percent of the (positive) part of the trade data,"

On Tuesday the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) released data showing the trade deficit for the first three months of the year was 40.2 billion crowns, up from 27.1 billion in the first quarter of 1996.
But the trade gap for March only of some 13.4 billion crowns was better-than-expected with some analysts forecasting a shortfall of as much as 18 billion crowns.
But Krovak said he saw no reason at this point to believe a long-term reversal of the widening trade deficit was occuring.
"Our forecast for the deterioration of the trade balance by about 50 percent compared to 1996 remains the same despite the figures in March," he said.
The 1996 trade deficit was a record 160.3 billion crowns.
